candidates.statement: The stakeholder uses the social network web application daily for news browsing and general scrolling for daily information.
context: Daily, routine use of the application

evidence_candidates.quote: So I daily use social network web application for like news browsing.
I just do general scrolling for daily information from them.

candidates.statement: Sometimes searches for job posting information on the application.
context: Occasional rather than daily

evidence_candidates.quote: And sometimes I search for job posting information.

candidates.statement: Does not want to miss important information such as major international events or new job postings.
candidates.modality: explicit avoidance ('I do not want to')
context: Examples given: international events and new job postings

evidence_candidates.quote: I do not want to miss out any important information like if there are any great events going on internationally.
maybe there are some new job posting

candidates.statement: The AI algorithm records likes and comments and recommends content based on the user's taste; described as the necessary feature for social applications.
context: Recommendation is fed by recorded likes, comments and browsing behaviour

evidence_candidates.quote: when I click likes, and when I comment on the postings of applications, they will record my actions, and after that they will do more like recommendations based on my. on my taste.
I think this is the necessary feature for social applications.

candidates.statement: Scrolls up and down on the main page to locate intended postings.
context: One of two main actions the user reports for information browsing

evidence_candidates.quote: When I enter the main page of social application. They would just show a bunch of postings to me, and I can just scroll up and down to to try to locate my intended postings.

candidates.statement: Uses the daily news ranking to go in and select the specific news wanted.
context: The other main action for information browsing

evidence_candidates.quote: So I can go into the ranking of the news and select the specific news I want.

candidates.statement: Uses the search bar at the top, types what to search, and receives results.
context: Unsure whether scrolling counts as a feature; search is named as another feature

evidence_candidates.quote: they have a search bar on the top, and I can just click the search bar and type in whatever I want to search. and they will give me the results.

candidates.statement: When searching by a specific region, there is no way to get information and results for that region; the user calls this a problem.
context: Results are described as returned randomly

evidence_candidates.quote: when I want to a like search. search some information based on a specific region. There is no way for me to get the get the information and results for that specific region.

candidates.statement: Would prefer a specific button or feature that allows searching in a specific region such as the city.
candidates.modality: preference ('it would be better for me')
context: Example: house rentals in a city

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be better for for me if there is a specific specific button, or or some feature in the application that I could search in a specific region like the city.

candidates.statement: Other ways such as housing agencies exist, but free social platforms are the only free way to deal with this.
context: Alternative channels are paid

evidence_candidates.quote: I can have other ways like I can go to the housing agencies. But anyway, these social platforms, they are free. So this is kind of the only free way that I can deal with this.

candidates.statement: Confirms wanting limitations or conditions added when searching.
context: Answer to interviewer question about adding search conditions

evidence_candidates.quote: So do you mean you want to like add some limitations or the conditions when searching the.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.

candidates.statement: Job listing search has fewer problems than housing rentals because AI recommendations push the right postings.
context: Comparison between job postings and housing rental postings

evidence_candidates.quote: because it can push you the right postings with artificial intelligence, recommendations.

candidates.statement: Housing rental postings lack a way to narrow the region, so many useful postings are filtered out.
context: Same comparison, housing side

evidence_candidates.quote: They don't have a a way to narrow the the region of the contents, so it just it will like filter out.

candidates.statement: Wants to see how many people are already entering the hiring process, to judge whether the company is hiring in large numbers.
candidates.modality: tentative want ('I might want to see')
context: Job search information need

evidence_candidates.quote: how how many people are already entering the hiring process, so that I can see if this company is on a great number of hiring or not

candidates.statement: Wants feedback from people who recently interviewed at the company, to judge whether its interview benchmark is high.
context: Job search information need

evidence_candidates.quote: I'll get feedback from the interviewees who just recently has taken the interviews from the company, and I can get feedback from them to see if this company is, does it have a high benchmark to to pass the interview or not?

candidates.statement: The general job-search experience is good for the user.
context: Answer to whether any challenge was met during job searching

evidence_candidates.quote: I think the general experience is good for me.

candidates.statement: Would prefer a feature that splits entertainment content from useful content during job and housing searches.
context: Entertainment and useful postings are currently pushed together

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be better if it it can have a feature that you can split the entertainment contents from useful contents like when you are doing the including job searching and housing rental, searching whatever.

candidates.statement: Wants entertainment content filtered out when the user does not want to see it.
candidates.modality: preference ('it would be better' / 'they can filter them out for me')
context: Conditional on the user not wanting entertainment content

evidence_candidates.quote: when sometimes I don't wanna see those entertainment contents, and they can filter them up for me.

candidates.statement: Also uses the application for entertainment such as daily jokes pushed to the user.
context: Answer to what other objectives the user has besides information browsing

evidence_candidates.quote: Also, maybe some like entertainment stuff like they will just push you some daily jokes for you.

candidates.statement: Entertainment content comes as photos and texts on this application, while other networks use videos.
context: Description of content format

evidence_candidates.quote: it will be in a form of photos and texts

candidates.statement: Values that AI applications continuously push the latest information fitting the user's taste without active searching.
context: Contrast with older search-only behaviour

evidence_candidates.quote: you can just stay there, and they will give you the the latest information. That fits your taste continuously.

candidates.statement: Knows personal data has been leaked and sold by apps and finds it risky, but has got used to it.
context: Prior experience with data leaks

evidence_candidates.quote: I know that my data has been leaked before, and it's quite quite risky.

candidates.statement: Accepts data leakage as unavoidable and tolerates it as long as it does not cause too much damage; would take legal action if this were found.
context: Not currently annoyed by the leaks

evidence_candidates.quote: as long as they wouldn't do too much damage to me. Or I haven't found that but once I found that I will like. take the lawsuit actions.

candidates.statement: Is good with the privacy issue and says it does not affect the general user experience.
context: Answer to whether the issue influences user experience

evidence_candidates.quote: I think I'm good with it. Yeah.

candidates.statement: Does not care much about the privacy issue.
context: Follow-up to the previous answer

evidence_candidates.quote: Don't care much about it.

candidates.statement: Suggests the company might improve its management to ensure it will not sell data to other parties.
context: Answer to what the company could do about the privacy issue

evidence_candidates.quote: They might just improve their management to ensure that they won't sell data to other parties.

candidates.statement: Says it is hard to tell which in-app features could protect privacy, because applications read data for better user experience and that is unavoidable.
context: Narrowed question about in-application privacy features

evidence_candidates.quote: I think it's hard to tell, because when when you are using applications, it just they they will read your data for for better user experience.

candidates.statement: Says social application platforms should strengthen efforts to handle matrix accounts that post identical marketing content and flood the feed with irrelevant content, interfering with user experience.
candidates.modality: recommendation ('should be done by the development team')
context: Open question about anything else the interviewer should know

evidence_candidates.quote: the social application platforms should strengthen their efforts to handle with matrix accounts.
they just flood the feed with irrelevant contents, and it interferes with user experience.
